rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear and humility are visible in believers’ gait and gestures, while the arrogant stiffen their bodies and stamp as they walk.
rows.anchor: people who have the fear of God in them are humble and down to earth. The affects of this humility are evident in their gait

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative ذَٰلِكَ refers to the Qur’an, the guidance God revealed and uses to guide whom He wills.
rows.anchor: In other words, this Qur’ān is the guidance revealed by God; through it, He guided whomsoever He wanted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God follows an established practice in granting guidance according to who is worthy of receiving it; those unworthy remain deprived.
rows.anchor: What is implied is that the Almighty adheres to a certain established practice regarding giving guidance.

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In keeping with that practice, no one can guide a person unworthy of guidance.
rows.anchor: in accordance with the above mentioned practice of God no one can guide a person who is not worthy of being guided.

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement also assures the Prophet that he need not fret over such people.
rows.anchor: These words actually sound an assurance to the Prophet (sws): he should not fret over such people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enunciative khabar is suppressed in the interrogative sentence, and Islahi supplies it in his translation.
rows.anchor: The enunciative ( khabar) in this interrogative sentence also is suppressed. I have tried to unfold it in the translation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment will be so terrible that the arrogant will try to use their faces as shields, with no other protection available.
rows.anchor: compelled to put forth their faces as their shields – faces with which they used to show arrogance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face is a person’s most valued and protected part, making its use as a shield an especially stark reversal.
rows.anchor: The noblest and dearest part of a person’s body is his face.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are the arrogant people who rejected the Qur’an and thereby wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: refers to the arrogant people under discussion. This is because by rejecting the Qur’ān they were guilty of wronging their souls.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will show no mercy at the helplessness of wrongdoers when they face punishment.
rows.anchor: The verse states that the Almighty will not have any mercy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses warn Quraysh not to treat the threatened punishment as a joke just because they currently live comfortably.
rows.anchor: These verses sound a warning to the Quraysh that they should not think that the punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier arrogant peoples also rejected their messengers, then were seized by punishment from an unexpected direction.
rows.anchor: Nations which preceded them also continued to deny their respective messengers because of this same malady of arrogance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s established practice is to destroy a nation that persists in rejecting its messenger after the truth has been conclusively conveyed; the Hereafter’s punishment is harder still.
rows.anchor: a nation that persists in denying its messenger is necessarily destroyed by the Almighty once the truth has been conclusively conveyed to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression means advice and wisdom given through parables; Islahi notes that the idiom can also describe wise statements made without a parable.
rows.anchor: The expression  ضرب مثل  means “to state sound advice and wisdom in the form of parables.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parables help people grasp facts, especially facts about the unseen, so God’s prophets use them often.
rows.anchor: Parables are very effective in making people understand certain facts – especially facts that relate to an unseen world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah, Gospel, and Psalms are full of parables, and Solomon’s scripture is called Proverbs.
rows.anchor: The Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms – all are replete with parables, and name of the scripture of Solomon is “Proverbs”.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is in an Arabic dialect especially suited to Arabs, free of complexity, eloquent, and expressed simply and effectively.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has revealed this Qur’ān in an Arabic dialect free from any complexity; it is in an eloquent tongue

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an teaches everything people need for success in this life and the Hereafter; neglecting it spurns God’s greatest favor and merits punishment after decisive communication.
rows.anchor: in a simple yet effective way instructs people of all the important things needed for success in this world and in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first stated aim of the Qur’an’s detailed parables is to remind people sunk in indifference.
rows.anchor: those who are deep in indifference may receive a reminder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second aim is to make people guard themselves from the punishment their indifference entails in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: The second objective is that they save themselves from the punishment which is the essential consequence of this indifference

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable maps a polytheist to a slave with many masters of different aims and a monotheist to a slave with one master.
rows.anchor: A polytheist is like a slave who has many masters each having different intents and objectives

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question implies that the two slaves are unequal; no one would choose several rival masters with conflicting aims.
rows.anchor: no slave will be prepared to be in the simultaneous ownership of many masters who not only have different intents but are also at war

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature is content with one God because human needs cannot be met without Him.
rows.anchor: Man’s nature feels content to be a slave to one God because his needs and deficiencies cannot be fulfilled without believing in Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one God fulfills a person’s needs, there is no reason to serve other gods; doing so rebels against human nature and entangles a person in an irrational predicament.
rows.anchor: As far as other gods are concerned, why should he become a slave to them if his needs are fulfilled by the one God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word tashākus means disagreement, so the associated gods are described as having conflicting aims.
rows.anchor: The word َسَاكَشَت points to an important psychological fact: It means َفَالَخَت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes associates whose purposes conflict with one another.
rows.anchor: The expression ُءَكاَرُش َونَسِاكَشَتُم  would mean associates which have conflicting objectives

rows.speaker: Idolaters
rows.claim: Idolaters believe their deities are hostile and jealous rivals who sometimes fight one another for ages.
rows.anchor: the Idolaters also believed that their deities are continuously in conflict and enmity with one another; they also feel jealous of one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Serving such rival deities humiliates a person; an idolater’s acceptance of this shows a loss of integrity and human dignity.
rows.anchor: Human nature will never be prepared to go through this humiliation; however, an Idolater will tolerate this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the parable’s question: He alone deserves gratitude, worship, and obedience because He bestowed all favors and did not authorize partners.
rows.anchor: All the favours have been given by Him; hence people should only thank Him and only worship Him and show obedience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth that only God deserves gratitude is clear, yet most people do not understand it.
rows.anchor: this fact is absolutely evident; however, a majority of people do not understand it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A psychological case for tawhid is that people are naturally courageous and resist being anyone’s slave.
rows.anchor: Man by his nature is someone who has great courage; he is never prepared to become the slave of anyone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People accept servitude to one God because it is innate and they need His support; an uncorrupted nature recoils from servitude to others.
rows.anchor: He becomes a slave to one God because, as pointed out earlier, this slavery is innately found in his nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says he explains this psychological argument in detail in his book Haqīqat-i shirk o tawhīd.
rows.anchor: which I have explained in detail in my book,  H@aqīqat-i shirk o tawh@īd.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses assure the Prophet and his companions and warn their enemies that the dispute over tawhid will ultimately be brought before God.
rows.anchor: this issue of tawh@īd which is under discussion will one day be presented in the court of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his enemies will both die and then appear before God as opposing parties in a case.
rows.anchor: Then both of them shall be presented in the court of God as two contestants of a case.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will ask the Prophet what he conveyed and ask the enemies how they responded before delivering the final verdict on who was right.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) will be asked what he taught and communicated to them; they will be asked about the response they gave.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet need not grieve over their stubborn talk: Satan’s opportunity lasts only for a time, and the truth’s adherents will prevail in the end.
rows.anchor: It is the requirement of God’s wisdom that this should go on till a certain period of time; however, one day this respite is going to end

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gravest wrong is to fabricate a claim about God and then deny the Qur’an when it comes to correct that lie.
rows.anchor: who invented a falsehood against God, and when the Almighty revealed a truth to rectify this falsehood they denied it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inventing a falsehood against God refers to polytheists’ unsupported claim that God made their deities His partners.
rows.anchor: Inventing falsehood against God refers to polytheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth that was denied is the Qur’an, which resolves differences and presents the truth.
rows.anchor: The word قْدِّالص here refers to the Qur’ān because it has resolved all differences and presented the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘when it came’ marks decisive communication: doubt may excuse someone, but stubborn denial of a truth made plain is like denying the midday sun.
rows.anchor: if there is an element of doubt in a truth and as a result a person is deprived of it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question expects agreement that Hell should be the home of such determined disbelievers, which is what will happen.
rows.anchor: a person who has even a slight sense in him will acknowledge that Hell should be the abode of such people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle man is omitted before ṣaddaqa bihi in the sentence about those who attest to the truth.
rows.anchor: the particle  ْنَم is suppressed before َقَّدَص ِهِب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muttaqūn here means those protected from Hell’s torment.
rows.anchor: the word َونُقَّتُم here refers to protection from the torment of Hell.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group spared from Hell includes Muhammad, who brought the Qur’an, and those who affirmed its truth.
rows.anchor: The above sentence mentions the reward of the other group comprising the one who brought the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bāʾ indicates that they wholeheartedly professed faith in the Book.
rows.anchor: The preposition  ب afterَقَّدَص  indicates that these people whole-heartedly professed faith in this Book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous will have whatever they desire with God, with no impediment to its fulfillment.
rows.anchor: they will have everything with their Lord which they desire; no impediment will be left for their desires to be fulfilled.

rows.speaker: a group of sūfīs
rows.claim: A group of Sufis understand nearness to God as merging into the divine person.
rows.anchor: the highest status a person can attain is nearness to God and not merging in His person, as understood by a group of sūfīs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects fusion with God, holding that the highest attainable status is nearness to Him.
rows.anchor: the highest status a person can attain is nearness to God and not merging in His person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised reward is for those who practice religion properly; merely claiming faith in the Qur’an does not suffice.
rows.anchor: Not every one who claims to profess faith in the Qur’ān will deserve this fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At judgment God will remove the evil consequences of the deeds of those who practice religion properly and reward them fittingly.
rows.anchor: he will wipe away the evil consequences of the deeds of His servants who befittingly practice religion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present world is brief, whereas the divine reward and punishment discussed here belong to another world.
rows.anchor: This world has a very limited span and the reward and punishment discussed in this verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative terms for the worst and best deeds signal comparison with their eternal consequences.
rows.anchor: are used in comparison. What is implied is that the Almighty has prescribed a Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment enables God to shield the faithful from the darker consequences of their deeds and grant them the noblest results of their good deeds.
rows.anchor: so that He may protect those of His people who adhere to faith from the consequences of the darker aspects of his deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should consider the effects their deeds will have in the eternal life to come, not merely their immediate outcomes.
rows.anchor: this verse guides man that he should not merely consider the immediate effects and consequences of his deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section IV turns to assuring the Prophet against threats tied to false deities and summarises the themes of verses 36–52.
rows.anchor: The succeeding verses sound an assurance to the Prophet (sws): he should tell those people who are intimidating him through their deities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should know that only the Creator of the heavens and earth can harm or benefit him, so the deities used to intimidate him cannot do so.
rows.anchor: except for this Lord Who is the creator of the heavens and the earth no one can harm or give benefit to him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should tell his opponents to do what they will and continue his own work without inhibition.
rows.anchor: He should tell them to do whatever they like. The Prophet (sws) should do whatever he is doing without any inhibition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is responsible for himself, not for whether other people believe or disbelieve.
rows.anchor: he is only responsible for his own self; he is not responsible for the belief or disbelief of others

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should explain the reality of the alleged intercession on which his opponents rely.
rows.anchor: if they are relying on their alleged intercession, then he should explain its reality to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should explain the transient nature of worldly success to those who take pride in it.
rows.anchor: if they show arrogance on their worldly successes, then he should explain their transient nature to them.
